gp.text: Our gross profit margin was 30.3% in both 2026 and 2025. The gross profit margin for the current year was negatively impacted by 0.3% due to higher LIFO expense as compared to the prior year. This was offset by price contribution and channel execution, as well as favorable mix impacts from the growth in revenues in the Engineered Solutions segment.

oi.text: Our 2026 consolidated sales were $5.0 billion, an increase of $403.3 million or 8.8% compared to the prior year, with acquisitions contributing to sales growth by $142.2 million or 3.1% and favorable foreign currency translation of $15.9 million increasing sales by 0.3%. Excluding the impact of businesses acquired and foreign currency translation, sales increased $245.2 million or 5.4% during the year due to higher volumes of approximately $136.2 million and the remainder from positive price contribution. The Company generated operating income of $549.5 million, or operating margin of 11.1% of sales for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to operating income of $498.5 million, or operating margin of 10.9% o f sales in the prior year. The Company generated net income of $414.5 million and $393.0 million during the years ended June 30, 2026 an d 2025 , respectively. Our diluted earnings per share was $10.95 in 2026 compared to $10.12 in 2025.

nonop.text: The Company had net interest expense in 2026 of $7.9 million compared to net interest expense of $0.6 million in 2025 primarily reflecting higher net interest expense following the January 2026 maturity of our interest rate swap, as well as lower interest income on reduced cash balances as compared to the prior year.

net.text: As a result o f the factors discussed above, net income for 2026 increased $21.5 million from 2025. Diluted net income per share was $10.95 per share for 2026 compared to $10.12 per share for 2025, an increase of 8.2%.

ocf.text: Cash provided by operating activities during 2026 declined $8.3 million as compared to the prior year primarily due to an increase in working capital of $65.8 million offset by higher net income of $21.5 million and higher deferred tax provision of $32.6 million reflecting the reduction of the deferred tax asset associated with capitalized R&D costs due to changes from the OBBBA. The increase in working capital was primarily due to higher accounts receivable of $61.5 million due to stronger revenues generated in the second half of 2026 as compared to 2025.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued compensation
lines.why: Wages, bonuses and benefits earned but not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.name: Equity

s.t: Our operations are primarily based in the United States where 88% of our 2026 sales were generated.
In 2026, our Service Center segment represented 64% of our total sales, while our Engineered Solutions segment represented 36% of our total sales.

The Company generated operating income of $549.5 million, or operating margin of 11.1% of sales for the year ended June 30, 2026, compared to operating income of $498.5 million, or operating margin of 10.9% o f sales in the prior year.

As we operate throughout North America, Singapore, Australia and New Zealand, and approximately 12% of our 2026 net sales were generated outside the United States, foreign currency exchange rates can impact our financial position, results of operations, and competitive position.
Products we distribute are generally supplied to us by manufacturers whom we serve as a non-exclusive distributor.
Loss of key supplier authorizations, lack of product availability, or changes in distribution programs could adversely affect our sales and earnings.
Our business depends on maintaining an immediately available supply of various products to meet customer demand.

The loss of key supplier authorizations or a substantial decrease in the availability of their products (including due to supply chain disruptions, as noted above), could put us at a competitive disadvantage and have a material adverse effect on our business.
For example, key suppliers could change the
Our ability to pass along increases in our costs in a timely manner to our customers depends on our ability to execute pricing changes, market conditions, and contractual limitations.

We depend on information systems to, among other things, process customer orders, manage inventory and accounts receivable collections, purchase products, manage accounts payable processes, ship products to customers on a timely basis, maintain cost-effective operations, provide superior service to customers, conduct business communications, and compile financial results.
Our business depends on maintaining operating activity at our headquarters and distribution centers and being able to receive and deliver product in a timely manner.
Our ability to service our debt and fund our other liquidity needs will depend on our ability to generate cash in the future.
